public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in AI & Compute

data.narrative:
General Intuition operates in the AI & Software sector at an undisclosed stage. The relevant comp universe consists of one public peer (Palantir Technologies, ticker PLTR) and eight private companies, including Figure AI, Scale AI, Reflection AI, and Applied Intuition. This narrow universe reflects the specialized nature of frontier-tech software valuations.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this analysis. While twelve same-sector peers exist in AI & Software, filtering for matching stage, adjacent stage, or comparable valuation tier yielded fewer than three datapoints in any subcategory. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material bias and obscure the specific risk and growth profiles of frontier-tech software businesses, which command distinct valuation multiples relative to mature software comparables.

Without sufficient narrow-peer triangulation, a defensible valuation range cannot be established from the available data. The primary uncertainties are: General Intuition's specific stage and development metrics relative to the identified private peer set; comparable revenue multiples or growth-adjusted valuations from the private comps; and stage-appropriate discount rates relative to the single public comparable. Further diligence would require disclosure of the company's revenue, growth trajectory, and capital structure to enable meaningful benchmarking against peers like Applied Intuition or Figure AI.
